intro: This unit tells two old stories from Genesis. First comes Noah and his big boat. Then comes a tall tower in a city called Babel. In both stories, people make big choices. Some choices go wrong. Some go right.

You will read the stories from Genesis itself. You will meet an old book called 1 Enoch. You will meet a Jewish writer from long ago named Josephus. And you will hear how Bible scholars, like Michael Heiser, read these stories.
By the end, you will be able to retell both stories in order. You will know words like ark, covenant and nation. And you will think about taking turns, listening and being kind.
bigQuestion: When big choices go wrong in Genesis, what does the story say God does next?

the name 1 Enoch gives to the heavenly ones who chose wrong
an old book with stories about Enoch and the Watchers
the big wooden boat Noah built
a big, lasting promise
the city in Genesis 11 where the story says languages got mixed up

test.q: What does 1 Enoch say the sons of God in Genesis 6 were?
test.why: 1 Enoch says they were heavenly ones. It calls them the Watchers.
Genesis 6 says Noah built an ark, a big wooden boat.

test.q: What sign did God give Noah, the story says?
test.why: Genesis 9 says the rainbow is the sign of God's promise.

test.q: Which old book calls the heavenly ones Watchers?
test.why: 1 Enoch calls the heavenly ones from Genesis 6 the Watchers.

test.q: What happened at Babel, the story says?
choices: God mixed up the people's language
test.why: Genesis 11 says God mixed up their language at Babel.
A covenant is a big, lasting promise, like the rainbow promise in Genesis 9.

test.why: The song in Deuteronomy 32 tells how God split the people into nations.

test.q: Whom did God call right after the Babel story?

test.q: What does it mean to bless someone?
test.why: To bless means to do good for someone.

test.q: What is one kind thing to do when someone speaks a different language?
choices: Smile and show them with your hands
test.why: You can smile, point and show. You can learn one of their words.

write.prompt: Tell about one promise in this unit. Use Genesis 9:13–15 or Genesis 12:3. Say what the story says God promised, and to whom. Then tell how one reader thought about it, like Josephus, Paul in Galatians 3:8, or a Bible scholar.
tips: Name the book and chapter, like Genesis 9.
Say "the story says" or "some readers think."
Use a unit word, like covenant or bless.
Draw a picture first if it helps you plan.

title: Big Choices Go Wrong

chapters.title: Noah and the Rainbow Promise
chapters.bigQuestion: What does the story of Noah say about choices and promises?

story.title: A Rainbow After the Storm
story.kicker: The storm is over. A rainbow shines. Grandma has a story to tell.
paragraphs: Rain taps on the window. Thunder rumbles far away. Then the storm stops. Maya and her little brother Jon run to the window. The sun peeks out. A rainbow stretches across the sky. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple.

Grandma comes to look too. She smiles. "That reminds me of an old story," she says. "It is in the Bible, in a book called Genesis. It is the story of Noah." Maya and Jon sit on the rug. They love Grandma's stories.
Grandma tells how the world got full of unkindness. She tells how Noah listened to God. She tells about a big boat full of animals. Jon giggles at the animal part. "Two by two!" he says.
"And at the end," Grandma says, "the story says God put a rainbow in the sky. It was a sign of a promise." Maya looks back at the window. The rainbow is fading now. But she will remember the story.
story.think: Grandma says the rainbow was a sign of a promise. What is a promise you have made?

lessons.title: Some Heavenly Ones Chose Wrong
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 6 says some heavenly ones chose wrong and came down to earth.
reading: The Bible's first book is *Genesis*. Chapter 6 tells a short, puzzling story. It says the *sons of God* came down to earth. They chose wives from the people there.

Long ago, a Jewish writer named Josephus read this story. He said the sons of God were angels. The old book 1 Enoch says they were heavenly ones too. Some Bible scholars today, like Michael Heiser, think so as well.
Other readers see it another way. Some think the sons of God were people, not heavenly ones. Readers still talk about this story today.

words.d: the first book of the Bible
a name in Genesis 6; many old readers thought it meant heavenly ones in God's family

look.title: Genesis 6 in Easy Words
look.text: There were many people on the earth. The sons of God saw the daughters of people. They saw that they were lovely. They chose wives from among them.
look.cite: Genesis 6:1–2, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Who came to the earth in this story? What did they do?

check.q: What did the writer Josephus say the sons of God were?
check.why: Josephus, a Jewish writer from long ago, said the sons of God in Genesis 6 were angels.

check.q: Which book of the Bible tells this story?
check.why: The story is in Genesis, chapter 6. Genesis is the Bible's first book.

check.q: What do some other readers think?
choices: The sons of God were people
The sons of God were birds
The story is about a rainbow
check.why: Some readers think the sons of God were people, not heavenly ones.

lessons.title: A World Full of Hurting
lessons.mainIdea: The story says the world filled with hurting and unkindness.
reading: Genesis 6 says things on earth went wrong. People were not kind. They hurt each other. The story says the earth was full of *violence*. That means hurting.
The story says God saw it. God was sad in his heart. The story says God planned a new start for the world.
The old book 1 Enoch tells more. It says the heavenly ones taught people things that led to hurting. One wrong choice can lead to more.

words.d: hurting others on purpose
not gentle or caring toward others

look.title: Two Playgrounds
look.text: Look at two playgrounds. On the first one, kids push and grab. Someone is crying. On the second one, kids take turns on the slide. Two kids help a friend who fell down.
look.prompt: Which playground is more like the world the story says God wanted? Why?

check.q: What does the word violence mean?
check.why: Violence means hurting others on purpose. Genesis 6 says the earth was full of it.

check.q: How did God feel when he saw the hurting, the story says?
check.why: Genesis 6 says God was sad in his heart when he saw the hurting.

check.q: What does 1 Enoch say the heavenly ones did?
choices: Taught people things that led to hurting
check.why: 1 Enoch says the heavenly ones taught people things that led to hurting.

lessons.title: Noah Chose to Listen
lessons.mainIdea: In the story, Noah listened to God.
reading: One man was different. His name was *Noah*. Genesis 6 says Noah walked with God. That means he stayed close to God and listened.
The story says God told Noah a big flood was coming. God told Noah to build a big boat. The boat would keep Noah's family and many animals safe.
Noah did all that God told him. Genesis 6:22 says so. It can be hard to *listen* when others do not. Noah listened anyway.

words.d: a man in Genesis who listened to God and built a big boat
to hear and pay attention

look.title: Noah Did It All
look.text: Noah did everything God told him to do. He did just what God asked.
look.cite: Genesis 6:22, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What does this verse say Noah did?

check.q: What does "Noah walked with God" mean?
choices: He stayed close to God and listened
check.why: In Genesis 6, walking with God means staying close to God and listening.

check.q: What did God tell Noah to build?
check.why: The story says God told Noah to build a big boat to keep his family and the animals safe.

check.q: Which verse says Noah did all God told him?
check.why: Genesis 6:22 says Noah did everything God told him.

lessons.title: The Big Boat and the Animals
lessons.mainIdea: Noah built a big boat called an ark. Animals came in two by two.
reading: The big boat is called an *ark*. Genesis 6 says it was very long. It was made of wood. It had a roof, a door and three floors inside.
God told Noah to bring animals. Two of each kind came, a male and a female. Some kinds came in sevens. Noah brought food for everyone too.
Noah's family went in too. There was Noah and his wife. There were his three sons and their wives. That makes eight people.

words.d: the big wooden boat Noah built

look.title: Counting on the Ark
look.prompt: Which number is the biggest? What does it count?

check.q: What is an ark?
check.why: An ark is the big wooden boat Noah built in Genesis 6.

check.q: How many people were in Noah's family on the ark?
check.why: Noah, his wife, his three sons and their three wives make eight people.

check.q: How did most animals come to the ark?
check.why: Genesis 6 says two of each kind came, a male and a female.

lessons.title: Rain, Then a Dove
lessons.mainIdea: After the rain stopped, a dove brought Noah an olive leaf.
reading: The rain came. Genesis 7 says it fell for forty days and forty nights. Water covered the land. The ark floated on top. Noah's family was safe inside.
Then the rain stopped. The water went down slowly. Noah sent out a *dove*. It came back with an *olive* leaf in its beak. Now Noah knew. Dry land was coming back!
Noah waited for God to tell him. Then his family stepped out onto dry ground. The animals came out too.

words.d: a gentle gray or white bird
a small fruit that grows on a tree with thin green leaves

look.title: The Olive Leaf
look.text: Picture the ark resting on a mountain. The sky is quiet. A little dove flies back to the window. In its beak is a fresh green leaf.
look.prompt: What did the green leaf tell Noah?

check.q: How long did the rain fall in the story?
check.why: Genesis 7 says the rain fell for forty days and forty nights.

check.q: What did the dove bring back?
check.why: Genesis 8 says the dove came back with an olive leaf in its beak.

check.q: Why was the olive leaf good news?
choices: It meant dry land was coming back
check.why: A fresh leaf meant trees were out of the water. Dry land was coming back.

lessons.title: A Promise in the Sky
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 9 says God put a rainbow in the sky as a sign of his promise.
reading: Noah and his family stood on dry land. Then, the story says, God made a *promise*. God promised never again to cover the whole earth with a flood.
God gave a sign of the promise. The sign was a *rainbow* in the clouds. The story says when the rainbow shows, God will remember his promise.
In the Bible, a big promise like this is called a *covenant*. The story says this one was for Noah, his family and every living thing.

words.d: saying you will surely do something
an arc of colors in the sky after rain
a big, lasting promise

look.title: The Bow in the Cloud
look.text: I put my bow in the cloud. It is the sign of my promise with the earth. When the bow is in the cloud, I will remember my promise.
look.cite: Genesis 9:13–15, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What does God say the bow in the cloud is a sign of?

check.q: What did God promise in Genesis 9, the story says?
choices: Never again to cover the whole earth with a flood
To send a dove every day
check.why: Genesis 9 says God promised never again to cover the whole earth with a flood.

check.q: What was the sign of the promise?
check.why: Genesis 9 says the rainbow in the clouds is the sign of the promise.

check.q: What is a covenant?
check.why: In the Bible, a covenant is a big, lasting promise, like the one in Genesis 9.

lessons.title: The Book of Enoch
lessons.mainIdea: An old book called 1 Enoch tells more about the heavenly ones. It calls them Watchers.
reading: Genesis 5 tells about a man named Enoch. He lived long before Noah. He was Noah's great-grandfather. The Bible says Enoch walked with God.
Long ago, people wrote an old book about Enoch. It is called *1 Enoch*. Most Bibles do not have it. The Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox churches keep it in their Bible.
1 Enoch tells more about the heavenly ones in Genesis 6. It calls them *Watchers*. Very old pieces of this book were found in caves near the Dead Sea. Many scholars study it today.

words.d: an old book with stories about Enoch and the Watchers
the name 1 Enoch gives to the heavenly ones who chose wrong

look.title: From Enoch to Noah
look.prompt: How many steps is it from Enoch to Noah?

check.q: What does 1 Enoch call the heavenly ones who chose wrong?
check.why: 1 Enoch calls the heavenly ones from Genesis 6 the Watchers.

check.q: Who was Enoch to Noah?
check.why: Genesis 5 goes from Enoch to Methuselah to Lamech to Noah. Enoch was Noah's great-grandfather.

check.q: Where were very old pieces of 1 Enoch found?
choices: In caves near the Dead Sea
check.why: Very old pieces of 1 Enoch were found in caves near the Dead Sea.

lessons.title: God Keeps Promises
lessons.mainIdea: Both old books say God set things right. The story says God keeps his promises.
reading: 1 Enoch chapter 10 tells how God sends good *angels* to help. God tells Noah to get ready. God stops the Watchers from doing more wrong. Then the book looks ahead to a clean, new start.
In Genesis, the rainbow shows up again and again. Each time, the story says, God remembers his promise. Many Jews and Christians see the rainbow as a *reminder* of it.
A promise is something you can count on. Keeping a promise shows care. You can keep promises too, like helping at home or being a good friend.

words.d: heavenly helpers and messengers
something that helps you remember

look.title: Lena's Promise
look.text: Lena told her little sister, "I will read to you tonight." At bedtime Lena is tired. She wants to sleep. Then she remembers her promise. She gets the book and reads.
look.prompt: How did Lena keep her promise? How do you think her sister felt?

check.q: In 1 Enoch, whom does God send to help?
check.why: 1 Enoch tells how God sends good angels to help and to set things right.

check.q: What does the rainbow help people remember, in the story?
check.why: Genesis 9 says the rainbow is a sign of God's promise.

check.q: What is a reminder?
check.why: A reminder helps you remember. Many readers see the rainbow as a reminder of the promise.

review.q: Who listened to God and built the ark?
review.why: Genesis 6 says Noah listened to God and built the ark.

review.q: What was the sign of God's promise to Noah?
review.why: Genesis 9 says the rainbow in the clouds is the sign of the promise.

review.q: What does 1 Enoch call the heavenly ones who chose wrong?
Josephus and 1 Enoch say the sons of God in Genesis 6 were what?
review.why: Josephus called them angels, and 1 Enoch calls them heavenly ones, the Watchers.

review.q: What did the dove bring back to Noah?
review.why: Genesis 8 says the dove came back with an olive leaf.

review.q: Which book of the Bible tells about Noah?
review.why: Noah's story is in Genesis, chapters 6 to 9.

chapters.title: The Tall Tower and Many Nations
chapters.bigQuestion: What happened at the tall tower, and how does the story say God planned to bless every nation?

story.title: The Block Tower
story.kicker: Three friends want to build the tallest tower ever. First they have to find a way to share.
paragraphs: It is block time in Room 12. Sofia, Ben and Amir want to build a tower. A tall one! They want it to touch the ceiling. They pull out every block in the bin.

But they cannot agree. Sofia wants only red blocks. Ben wants to build fast. Amir is still learning English. He tries to say an idea, but the others do not understand. Everyone talks at once. The tower wobbles. Then it falls down.
Their teacher, Ms. Lee, sits down with them. "What if you take turns?" she asks. "And what if you listen?" Amir shows them with his hands. He wants a wide bottom, so the tower will stand.
They try again. Each child adds one block. Then the next child adds one. Amir teaches them a word from his home language. The new tower is not the tallest. But it stands, and they built it together.
story.think: How did taking turns and listening help the three friends?

lessons.title: Let's Build a Tower!
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 11 says people built a city and a tall tower to reach the sky.
reading: After the flood, Noah's family grew and grew. Genesis 11 says everyone spoke one *language*. They all used the same words.
The people found a flat land called Shinar. They made bricks and baked them hard. They said, let us build a city and a tall *tower*. Let its top reach the sky.
They wanted to make a big name for themselves. They did not want to spread out over the earth. But God had told people to fill the earth.

words.d: the words people use to talk to each other
a tall, narrow building

look.title: Let Us Build
look.text: Come, let us make bricks. Let us build a city and a tower with its top in the sky. Let us make a name for ourselves, so we are not spread out over the whole earth.
look.cite: Genesis 11:3–4, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: What did the people want? Name two things.

check.q: How many languages did people speak at the start of Genesis 11?
check.why: Genesis 11 says everyone spoke one language.

check.q: What did the people want to build?
choices: A city and a tall tower
check.why: Genesis 11 says they wanted to build a city and a tower that reached the sky.

check.q: What did the people not want to do?
check.why: The people said they did not want to be spread out over the whole earth.

lessons.title: Mixed-Up Words
lessons.mainIdea: The story says God mixed up their language and spread the people over the earth.
reading: Genesis 11 says God came down to see the city and the tower. God saw what the people were doing.
Then, the story says, God mixed up their language. One person said a word. The next person did not understand it. They could not work together on the tower.
So the people stopped building. They had to *scatter* to many places. The city was called *Babel*. The name sounds like a Hebrew word that means to mix up.

words.d: the city in Genesis 11 where the story says languages got mixed up
to spread out in many directions

look.title: Say It Another Way
look.text: Try this. Say "hello" to a friend. Now think of other ways people say it. "Hola" in Spanish. "Bonjour" in French. "Ni hao" in Chinese. Same idea, different words.
look.prompt: Why was it hard for the people at Babel to keep building?

check.q: What did God do to the people's language, the story says?
check.why: Genesis 11 says God mixed up their language, so they could not understand each other.

check.q: What was the city called?
check.why: The city was called Babel. Shinar was the name of the flat land where it stood.

check.q: What happened after the language got mixed up?
choices: People moved away to many places
check.why: The story says the people stopped building and spread out to many places.

lessons.title: Families Become Nations
lessons.mainIdea: Families spread out and became many nations with many languages.
reading: Genesis 10 is a long list of names. It shows how Noah's family grew. Noah's sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth. Their children had children, and on and on.
Each big family became a *nation*. A nation is a large group of people. They share a land and often a language. Jewish tradition counts seventy nations in the list.
Today the world has about 7,000 languages. Some are spoken by millions of people. Some are spoken by only a few. Each one is a way to share ideas.

words.d: a large group of people who share a land and often a language

look.title: From One to Many
rows: Languages at the start of Genesis 11
look.cite: Genesis 10:1 and 11:1; the count of 70 is traditional
look.prompt: The story starts with one language. How many nations are in the list?

check.q: What were the names of Noah's three sons?
check.why: Genesis 10 says Noah's sons were Shem, Ham and Japheth.

check.q: What is a nation?
choices: A large group of people who share a land
check.why: A nation is a large group of people who share a land and often a language.

check.q: About how many languages are in the world today?
check.why: The world has about 7,000 languages today.

lessons.title: Heavenly Ones Over the Nations
lessons.mainIdea: Deuteronomy 32 says God split up the nations. Old copies link them to the sons of God.
reading: *Deuteronomy* 32 is a song in the Bible. It tells how God split the people into nations. It says God gave each nation its own land.

Very old copies of this song were found near the Dead Sea. One says God set the nations by the number of the *sons of God*. The old Greek Bible, the *Septuagint*, says angels of God. Many Bibles say sons of Israel.
Some Bible scholars, like Michael Heiser, think God let heavenly ones watch over the nations for a time. But God kept one people for himself. Other readers think the verse is only about people.

words.d: the fifth book of the Bible
a Bible name; many readers think it means heavenly ones in God's family
a very old Greek copy of the Hebrew Bible

look.title: The Song in Deuteronomy
look.text: When the Most High gave the nations their lands, he set their borders by the number of the sons of God. But the LORD kept his own people for himself.
look.cite: Deuteronomy 32:8–9, paraphrased from a Dead Sea Scroll reading; the Septuagint (Brenton, 1844) has "angels of God"; the King James Version (1611) has "children of Israel"
look.prompt: Whom does this song say God kept for himself?

check.q: What does the old Greek Bible, the Septuagint, say in this verse?
check.why: The Septuagint says God set the nations by the number of the angels of God.

check.q: Where was one very old copy of this song found?
check.why: One very old copy of Deuteronomy 32 was found near the Dead Sea.

check.q: What do many Bibles say in this verse instead of sons of God?
check.why: Many Bibles, like the King James Version, say sons or children of Israel in this verse.

lessons.title: God Calls Abram
lessons.mainIdea: Right after Babel, Genesis tells how God chose one man, Abraham, to start a new family.
reading: Genesis 11 ends with a family from a city called Ur. One man in that family was Abram. Later God gave him a new name, *Abraham*.
In Genesis 12, God spoke to Abram. God said, leave your home and go to a new land. I will show it to you. Abram listened. He packed up and went.
Look where this story sits. It comes right after Babel. The people at Babel wanted a big name. In Genesis 12:2, God says he will make Abram's name great.

words.d: the man God called in Genesis 12; his first name was Abram

look.title: Abram Sets Out
rows: Genesis chapter where God calls Abram
Abram's age when he set out
look.cite: Genesis 11–12; Abram's age is from Genesis 12:4
look.prompt: How old was Abram when he set out? How close are the Babel chapter and the Abram chapter?

check.q: What was Abraham's first name?
check.why: Genesis says his first name was Abram. Later God gave him the name Abraham.

check.q: What did God tell Abram to do in Genesis 12?
choices: Leave home and go to a new land
check.why: In Genesis 12, God told Abram to leave his home and go to a new land.

check.q: What does God say he will make great in Genesis 12:2?
check.why: In Genesis 12:2, God says he will make Abram's name great. At Babel, people tried to make a name for themselves.

lessons.title: A Blessing for Every Nation
lessons.mainIdea: Genesis 12:3 says all the families of the earth would be blessed through Abraham.
reading: God made Abram a big promise. Genesis 12 says God would make his family into a great nation. And more. Through him, all the families of the earth would be *blessed*.
To *bless* means to do good for someone. So the promise was not just for one family. It reached out to every nation, even the ones spread out at Babel.

Later, the New Testament points back to this promise. Galatians 3:8 calls it good news for the nations. Many Christians read it this way. Jewish tradition honors Abraham as the father of the Jewish people.

words.d: to do good for someone
given good things; cared for

look.title: A Promise for All Families
look.text: I will bless those who bless you. And in you, all the families of the earth will be blessed.
look.cite: Genesis 12:3, paraphrased from the King James Version (1611)
look.prompt: Who does this promise say will be blessed?

check.q: In Genesis 12:3, who would be blessed through Abram?
choices: All the families of the earth
check.why: Genesis 12:3 says all the families of the earth would be blessed through him.

check.q: What does it mean to bless someone?
check.why: To bless means to do good for someone.

check.q: Which New Testament book points back to this promise?
check.why: Galatians 3:8 points back to the promise that all nations would be blessed through Abraham.

lessons.title: Taking Turns and Listening
lessons.mainIdea: Taking turns and listening help people work together.
reading: At Babel, the people wanted a big name for themselves. Then the story says their words got mixed up. They could not understand each other. The work stopped.
Working together takes care. It helps to *take turns*. It helps to *listen* all the way to the end. Then everyone gets a say.
Think of a class building a tower of blocks. One child adds a block. Then the next child does. Everyone waits. The tower grows, one turn at a time.

words.d: to let each person have a go, one after another
to hear and pay attention

look.title: The Lunch Table
look.text: Look at the lunch table. Three friends want to tell a story at the same time. Nobody can hear. Then Kai says, "You go first." Each friend tells a story. Everyone laughs.
look.prompt: What helped the friends hear each other?

check.q: What does it mean to take turns?
choices: Let each person have a go, one after another
Only one person ever gets a go
check.why: Taking turns means each person has a go, one after another.

check.q: At Babel, what did the people want for themselves?
check.why: Genesis 11 says the people wanted to make a big name for themselves.

check.q: What helps a group work together?
check.why: Taking turns and listening all the way to the end help everyone get a say.

lessons.title: Kind to Every Language
lessons.mainIdea: People speak many languages. You can be kind to people who speak differently.
reading: In Chicago and all over Illinois, families speak many languages. You might hear Spanish, Polish, Arabic or Chinese on the bus. Each language comes from a family's story.
Someone may speak a language you do not know. You can still be *kind*. You can smile. You can point and show. You can learn one of their words.
The Babel story ends with people far apart. Abraham's story starts a promise to bless every nation. Being kind to people from every nation fits that promise well.

words.d: gentle and caring toward others

look.title: A New Friend
look.text: A new girl joins the class. She speaks Polish. She is still learning English. At recess she stands by the fence. Theo walks over. He smiles and holds out a ball.
look.prompt: What else could Theo do to help his new friend feel welcome?

check.q: What can you do if someone speaks a language you do not know?
choices: Smile and show them with your hands
check.why: You can smile, point and show. You can learn one of their words.

check.q: Which promise reached out to every nation?
choices: The plan to build a tower
The plan to build an ark
God's promise to Abraham in Genesis 12:3
check.why: Genesis 12:3 says all the families of the earth would be blessed through Abraham.

check.q: Which is a language many families speak in Chicago?
check.why: Many Chicago families speak Spanish. Babel is a city in the story, and Shinar is a land.

review.q: Which chapter of Genesis tells about the tall tower?
review.why: The tower story is in Genesis 11.

review.q: What was the city with the tower called?
Whom did God call to start a new family?
review.why: In Genesis 12, God called Abram, later named Abraham.

review.q: Where were very old copies of the song in Deuteronomy 32 found?
review.why: Very old copies of Deuteronomy 32 were found near the Dead Sea.

choices: A tower that reaches the sky
All the families of the earth will be blessed
review.why: Genesis 12:3 says all the families of the earth would be blessed through Abraham.
Taking turns and listening help everyone get a say.
